summary_of_threads_started_this_week:
NestedMuSig2 introduces a hierarchical, privacy-preserving multi-signature approach that allows subgroups to participate with aggregate public keys while generating a single BIP340-compatible signature. The proposal, detailed in both a [BIP draft](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/pull/2297) and [academic paper](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/223), seeks feedback on nonce handling, session design, and integration with BIP327, with the reference implementation available for review.

A new draft standardizes transaction inclusion proofs using wtxid, consolidating various formats across projects and providing [reference implementations](https://github.com/jeanpablojp/bips/blob/witness-inclusion-proofs/bip-witness-inclusion-proofs.md) and test vectors for validation. The draft explores complexities in Merkle branch verification, proposes explicit segwit activation inputs, and describes two proof formats to ensure compatibility and security for lightweight and full nodes.

Bitcoin Core has released versions [30.5](https://bitcoincore.org/bin/bitcoin-core-30.5/) and [31.3](https://bitcoincore.org/bin/bitcoin-core-31.3/) with bug fixes, performance improvements, updated translations, and enhanced transaction inventory processing, addressing a medium-severity security vulnerability as detailed in the [security advisory](https://bitcoincore.org/en/2026/11/20/disclose-orphan-inv-stall/). Community contributions by fanquake, Greg Sanders, willcl-ark, and others are acknowledged, with [community engagement](https://bitcoincore.org/en/list/announcements/join/) encouraged via mailing lists and issue trackers.

Recent proposals advance the integration of mnemonic-based wallet recovery into descriptors ([pull request](https://github.com/polespinasa/bips/pull/2)), improve multisig session security via [formal protocols](https://github.com/KeylayBTC/msp), and introduce the Node Attestation Protocol ([satd 0.7+](https://github.com/epochbtc/satd)), enabling economic nodes to cryptographically signal support for network changes while balancing privacy considerations.

Analyses of UTXO exposure ([extraction rules](https://github.com/duncan0k/btc-exposure-index/blob/2a0f4b053cad2ae3dc101a4e4c154ac2b4706f25/docs/extraction-rules.md11-relation-to-the-bip-362-draft)) and BIP54’s block timestamp consensus rules reveal both the scale of exposed BTC and nuanced security implications, including potential but impractical attack vectors. Post-quantum security remains a focal point, with new [PQ bridge designs](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/2877) and recovery frameworks ([shrinc-ray](https://gist.github.com/ajtowns/d6bfc7a2fa4a2fdfe9f8f79cf1e1db34)) under discussion to ensure Bitcoin’s resilience against future cryptographic threats.

new_threads_this_week.title: [BIP Draft] NestedMuSig2: Recursive MuSig2 for BIP340-compatible Signatures
new_threads_this_week.summary: - NestedMuSig2 enables hierarchical signing groups to collaboratively produce privacy-preserving BIP340-compatible signatures.  - The proposal emphasizes nonce management, session design, and BIP327 compatibility in recursive scenarios.  - Technical feedback and review of the specification, implementation, and test vectors are requested.

new_threads_this_week.title: [BIP Proposal] Witness Transaction Inclusion Proofs
new_threads_this_week.summary: - A draft proposes standardized transaction inclusion proofs using wtxid, consolidating varied existing approaches and implementations.  - Two proof formats are described, with differences in efficiency and compatibility with current Bitcoin tools.  - Explicit validation requirements, security recommendations, and pending design questions are outlined, inviting further feedback.

new_threads_this_week.title: Bitcoin Core v30.5 Released
new_threads_this_week.summary: - Bitcoin Core v30.5 offers bug fixes, performance boosts, and broader translation support for its users.  - Upgrading requires shutting down running instances, with migration support and ongoing backward compatibility.  - The release features networking and integration improvements, platform compatibility, and acknowledges contributor efforts.

new_threads_this_week.title: Bitcoin Core security advisory for an easily discoverable vulnerability
new_threads_this_week.summary: - Fixed releases for versions 31.3 and 30.5 address a medium severity security vulnerability.  - Version 32.1 already contains the security update and requires no user action.  - Users on version 29.x are strongly advised to upgrade to ensure continued security.

new_threads_this_week.title: Bitcoin Core v31.3 Released
new_threads_this_week.summary: - Bitcoin Core 31.3 features bug fixes, improved performance, and updated translations for enhanced stability.  - Users should carefully follow platform-specific upgrade steps and can report issues using the issue tracker.  - Official support is limited to recent Linux, macOS, and Windows versions, with contributions acknowledged.

new_threads_this_week.title: [BIP Draft] bip39() Descriptor Key Expression
new_threads_this_week.summary: - A new proposal introduces key expressions for integrating mnemonics into wallet output script descriptors.  - This enables more consistent, secure wallet recovery by including mnemonic details and relevant derivation data.  - The draft and initial implementation are available, with feedback welcomed through the provided discussion channels.

new_threads_this_week.title: How much BTC sits behind keys or scripts already on chain (block 975,019)
new_threads_this_week.summary: - Approximately 35.6% of Bitcoin unspent outputs are exposed based on public key or script disclosure.  - Key reuse analysis reveals significant overlaps, especially between P2PKH and P2WPKH output formats.  - Reference tables aid BIP 362 work, but measurement discrepancies and ambiguities remain in the current draft.

new_threads_this_week.title: Node Attestation Protocol
new_threads_this_week.summary: - Miner signaling has limitations, prompting the development of more inclusive mechanisms like the Node Attestation Protocol.  - NAP allows economic nodes to submit weighted, cryptographically verifiable attestations without requiring central trust.  - Attestations are non-binding, time-limited, and raise privacy concerns for coin holders despite their pseudonymous nature.

new_threads_this_week.title: Open Question on a hypothetical minor "slow-sliding MTP" attack introduced by BIP 54
new_threads_this_week.summary: - BIP54 introduces stricter block timestamp rules, focusing on security against adversarial manipulations.  - The protocol uses a wide acceptance window, limiting attack feasibility and maintaining network resilience.  - Sustained attacks require majority hash rate and offer minimal advantage, making exploitation highly impractical.

new_threads_this_week.title: Toward Efficient Post-Quantum Bitcoin Bridges
new_threads_this_week.summary: - A post-quantum garbled-circuit verifier for STARK proofs offers secure, efficient Bitcoin bridge deployments.  - Using binary fields and Blake3, this approach optimizes circuit size, input minimization, and computational efficiency.  - The design significantly reduces storage needs and transaction volume compared to previous solutions like BitVM3.

new_threads_this_week.title: Post Quantum Recovery Framework
new_threads_this_week.summary: - Quantum computers threaten Bitcoin security, requiring post-quantum recovery protocols to safeguard user assets.  - Recovery protocols must balance protecting funds from theft and avoiding permanent coin loss.  - Debate surrounds whether to use essential or accidental secrets, especially for multisignature wallet recovery methods.

new_threads_this_week.title: Multisig Session Protocol: draft spec for remote multisig setup and signing needs review
new_threads_this_week.summary: - A new open protocol enables secure remote multisig wallet setups, addressing critical security vulnerabilities.  - Mutual authentication uses short codes and nonces, safeguarding key exchanges even over untrusted channels.  - The protocol supports two or more cosigners, invites peer review, and remains under active technical development.

active_posts_this_week.title: [BIP Proposal] Stale Tip Relay
active_posts_this_week.summary: - Relaying stale block headers and data enhances research, transparency, and monitoring for consensus issues and attacks.  - Widespread stale block relay is unnecessary; selective, opt-in participation by a small network subset suffices.  - Stale block relay improves network analysis but should remain optional to balance utility, overhead, and security.

active_posts_this_week.title: Re: RFC: Two years of BIP Editing, time for some new faces?
active_posts_this_week.summary: - The BIP Editor team is struggling with an unsustainable workload and a growing review backlog.  - Strengthening the editorial team by appointing three new editors is strongly preferred over lowering standards.  - Limited terms of 12 to 24 months are encouraged to attract qualified volunteer editors.

active_posts_this_week.title: Quantum Landmines and Vulnerable Coin Auctions
active_posts_this_week.summary:
- Transferring assets to quantum-resistant wallets is advised for those aware of quantum computing risks.
- Keeping assets on legacy outputs without reason increases unnecessary risks and attracts malicious activity.
- Proactive protection ensures valuable assets are not susceptible to future quantum computing threats.

active_posts_this_week.title: BIP Proposal: ML-KEM Key Establishment
active_posts_this_week.summary: - A proposal introduces Hybrid Key Encapsulation using a UG combiner function within the Elements project.  - It integrates secp256k1 ECDH and ML-KEM-768 to provide resistance against chosen ciphertext attacks.  - This approach ensures post-quantum security while preserving backward compatibility with current cryptographic standards.

active_posts_this_week.title: Great Consensus Cleanup Revival
active_posts_this_week.summary: - The BIP54 modifications have been incorporated into libbitcoin, aligning it with the latest standards.  - Review and thorough testing are necessary to ensure the modifications’ accuracy and reliability.  - Validation will compare libbitcoin with Bitcoin Core to identify and address any inconsistencies.

active_posts_this_week.title: Unspendable keys in descriptors
active_posts_this_week.summary: - Maximalist normalization reduces redundancy and enhances data integrity but can complicate queries and aggregation.  - Selective normalization allows some redundancy to improve performance and simplify frequent queries.  - Minimal sorted unique keys optimize entity identification, index efficiency, and query performance.

active_posts_this_week.title: Bounds on chain length with BIP-54 timewarp fixes
active_posts_this_week.summary: - Bitcoin’s Difficulty Adjustment Algorithm faces challenges responding to sustained hash rate increases, risking block manipulation.  - Shortening the averaging window boosts responsiveness but may introduce instability to mining difficulty levels.  - A proposed modification aims to penalize accelerated blocks, improving accuracy but possibly increasing volatility.

active_posts_this_week.title: Propagation Delay and Mining Centralization: Modeling Stale Rates
active_posts_this_week.summary: - The mining simulation project now includes 2026 values and Fable's bug fixes for improved accuracy.  - README documentation has been expanded with analysis on stale rates and their impact on profitability.  - Potential internal delays and efficiency gains from Stratum V2 adoption are currently under consideration.

active_posts_this_week.title: Decentralized Coinbase Payout Protocols (DCPP): A Framework for Discussion
active_posts_this_week.summary: - Lithos Protocol delivers a decentralized, blockchain-agnostic solution for challenges in distributed mining pools.  - Its scalable architecture and optimized payout granularity enable efficient and streamlined distributions.  - Trustless bitcoin relay allows secure, transparent cross-chain block settlement with further details available online.

active_posts_this_week.title: PSBT/MuSig2 coordination over Nostr relays: transport invariants for nonce safety under at-least-once delivery
active_posts_this_week.summary: - Message identity relies on a truncated deterministic hash for uniqueness and robust duplicate detection.  - Session, round, and sender identity binding with monotonic sequencing assure integrity and reliability.  - Idempotence concerns remain due to non-explicit round handling, with explicit authentication under consideration.

active_posts_this_week.title: We made the bitcoin-dev mailing list readable: 15 years, 24,699 messages
active_posts_this_week.summary: - Segwit2x aimed to address block size limits and transaction throughput with two scaling approaches.  - Debate involved diverse stakeholders discussing technical feasibility, security, and impacts on decentralization.  - The proposal failed to achieve consensus, emphasizing the necessity of broad agreement for network changes.

active_posts_this_week.title: A STARK proof of Bitcoin's UTXO set at block 972,500, with circuits proven in Lean
active_posts_this_week.summary: - Two ConnectBlock rules, BIP68 and full sigop cost, are not currently enforced in the proof system.  - Proof verification is mostly limited by reading snapshots from disk, not by computational verification time.  - The modular proof system enables future improvements and formal analysis, focusing on robust UTXO set integrity.
